name: Months
overview: Scripture reveals that months were originally marked by the first appearance of the new moon, serving as a divine measure of time as established by God’s creation of the sun and moon to separate day from night and to signal seasons and years (Genesis 1:14). The patriarchs and later the Jewish people computed time by these lunar months, which initially had no names but later became identified by specific titles such as Nisan or Abib for the first month (Genesis 7:11; 8:4; Exodus 13:4). Observances tied to the beginnings of months were significant in Israel’s worship, as indicated by the blowing of trumpets at the start of months to commemorate sacred occasions before God (Numbers 10:10).
